outlook.statement: The Company's focus extends beyond responding to change—it is centred on anticipating it. By combining deep market insight, robust operating platforms, prudent risk management, and a culture of innovation, Emkay is building an organisation capable of scaling sustainably while adapting to the evolving needs of investors and markets.

As India advances towards becoming one of the world's leading economic powers, the financial services sector stands at the forefront of wealth creation, capital formation, and investment participation. Positioned at the intersection of these opportunities, Emkay continues to strengthen its research expertise, institutional, asset management and wealth management capabilities, and technology-led platforms to deliver differentiated value to clients.
Strengthening Capital Markets franchise through deepening institutional relationships and expanding research-led engagement across domestic and international markets
Building stronger mid-market Investment Banking pipeline across IPOs, QIPs and strategic advisory mandates
Scaling Wealth & Asset Management platforms with focus on HNI engagement, AUM expansion and differentiated investment offerings
Accelerating technology-led transformation with ongoing investments in digital infrastructure, automated risk management and scalable trading platforms
Enhancing global investor outreach across Singapore, Dubai, US and other strategic international markets
Maintaining strong governance & risk discipline with focus on robust compliance frameworks, operational resilience and long-term value creation
2027-28 forward revenue pipeline for Investment Banking projected above ₹100 Crores supported by growing mid-market corporate engagement programme
FII revenue share expected to grow over medium term with focused US footprint expansion
Asset management roadmap for 2026-27 targets further expansion into Bangalore and Chennai, scaling core strategies, and deepening presence across top-tier distribution platforms

Built for the Next Upcycle - Strong research franchise, diversified revenue streams and trusted client relationships position Emkay to capture the next phase of market growth. Growing domestic participation, increasing financialisation and institutional investor flows.

We extend our deepest gratitude to our clients, whose continued trust and partnership inspire us to raise our standards every year. We thank our Board of Directors for their commitment to delivering sustainable value, and we look forward to a stronger 2026-27, as we continue building the next chapter of Emkay's journey.

India's near-to medium-term growth outlook remains favourable, with economic momentum expected to stay resilient in 2026-27, supported by healthy domestic consumption, sustained investment activity, continued infrastructure spending and improving private sector participation. India's real GDP growth is projected to remain in the range of 6.80%–7.20% in 2026-27.

The outlook for Indian financial markets in 2026-27 remains cautiously optimistic, supported by strong domestic fundamentals, improving earnings expectations, policy easing, and sustained capital expenditure. Goldman Sachs upgraded Indian equities to “Overweight” and set a Nifty 50 target of 29,000 by December 2026, with financials, consumer staples, defence, and oil marketing companies expected to lead the next phase of growth.

India's wealth and asset management industry is entering a period of sustained expansion, supported by rising affluence, increasing financialisation, demographic shifts and technological innovation. Assets under management (AUM) are expected to increase from approximately US$1.1 trillion in FY24 to US$2.3 trillion by FY29, representing an incremental opportunity of nearly US$1.6 trillion.

India's wealth management industry entering its defining decade with economy projected to expand from ~USD 4 trillion to USD 30 trillion by 2047; HNI population expected to reach ~1.65 million by 2027, UHNI segment growing ~50% by 2028

Sustained capital-raising activity and expanding SME participation underscore increasing depth, accessibility, and maturity of India's capital markets; IPO volumes up 20%, funds raised up 10% in 2025-26 (up to Dec 2025); SME listings increased to 217 from 190, capital raised from ₹7,453 crore to ₹9,635 crore

PMS segment expanded from ₹1.27 lakh crore to ₹8.37 lakh crore (CAGR 20.75% over 10 years); AIF commitments surged from ₹27,484 crore to ₹15.05 lakh crore (CAGR 49.23%); 1,699 registered AIFs as of November 2025
Investment banking maintains robust deal visibility with projected revenue of ~₹100 crore over next 24 months
Resilient investor behaviour driving shift towards disciplined, long-term investing; record SIP inflows of ₹32,087 crore and net equity mutual fund inflows of ₹40,450 crore in March 2026

Your Company does not deal in any commodity and hence is not directly exposed to any commodity price risk.
The Company's foreign exchange risk is negligible and hence it has not undertaken any hedging activities.

The Company has in place a mechanism to inform the Board about the risk assessment and minimization procedures and periodical review to ensure that management controls risk through means of a properly defined framework.

Trade policy volatility remains a key macroeconomic risk. Unresolved issues around tariffs, export controls, and strategic supply chains may disrupt trade flows, create supply bottlenecks, and heighten inflationary pressures.

Fiscal and financial stability concerns persist amid elevated sovereign debt, widening fiscal deficits, and volatile debt markets. Abrupt yield movements or policy missteps could increase macro-financial stress.

Geopolitical tensions continue to cloud the global outlook. Escalating conflict in the Middle East, particularly involving Iran, Israel, and the United States, has heightened concerns around disruption of critical oil supply routes and commodity market volatility.

Near-term market sentiment may remain influenced by external headwinds, including escalating geopolitical tensions in West Asia, elevated crude oil prices, persistent FII outflows, rupee depreciation, uncertainty around US tariffs, and potential delays in interest rate cuts.
Sustained crude prices above USD 100 per barrel could impact India's inflation, current account, and corporate profitability, particularly across crude-sensitive sectors.
